cluster_summary: This cluster covers cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities arising from user-controlled data being inserted into the DOM via innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or markdown-to-HTML pipelines without proper sanitization or escaping. The root cause is the assumption that user input is safe for HTML context. Fix strategies range from using textContent or HTML encoding for plain text, adding DOMPurify or rehype-sanitize for HTML content, escaping attributes in custom renderers, to replacing dangerouslySetInnerHTML with JSX expressions or using DOM APIs with URL validation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations into redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets. Report code paths where the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization.

mechanism.missing_guard: the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values
mechanism.name: open redirect through unsafe URI scheme validation
mechanism.sink_shape: redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Post-process the generated HTML to strip event handler attributes (on*) and dangerous URI schemes (javascript:, data:text/html).
sub_patterns.name: Missing HTML attribute escaping in string-concatenated HTML
sub_patterns.root_cause: User input inserted into attribute values via string interpolation without escaping quotes, allowing attribute injection and event handler injection.

sub_patterns.name: Unsanitized HTML injection in user-controlled content rendering
